text: Practical guidance: choose DMR for Docker-native workflows, OCI artifact distribution and CI (Testcontainers); choose Ollama for rapid prototyping, framework independence and a larger one-command model library. Some CUDA images reportedly hardcode a 4096-token context limit that overrides higher settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A single-hardware benchmark (M1 Pro, 50 runs each, model unnamed, March 2025) found DMR 24.53 vs Ollama 23.65 mean tokens/sec, a 0-12% per-prompt difference; the author calls them comparable. Variance was high and the setup was one machine. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-03)

DMR supports three inference engines: llama.cpp (default, GGUF, all platforms), vLLM (Safetensors, NVIDIA GPUs; Linux x86_64 and Windows WSL2) and Diffusers (image generation, NVIDIA on Linux). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
Models are pulled from Docker Hub, any OCI-compliant registry, or Hugging Face; GGUF and Safetensors files can be packaged as OCI artifacts and published to any registry. (high confidence)
DMR serves an OpenAI-compatible API and an Ollama-compatible API. The default local endpoint is http://localhost:12434/v1/chat/completions. (high confidence)

Engine routing is automatic by model format: a GGUF model uses llama.cpp, a Safetensors model uses vLLM. The vLLM backend is installed once with 'docker model install-runner --backend vllm --gpu cuda'. (medium confidence)

Docker announced the vLLM integration on 2025-11-20. At launch it supported only x86_64 with NVIDIA GPUs, had slower startup than llama.cpp, and few vLLM-format models on Docker Hub. Docker recommends prototyping on llama.cpp and scaling to vLLM. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-20)

Platform support: macOS needs Apple Silicon; Windows amd64 needs NVIDIA drivers 576.57+ (arm64 uses OpenCL on Adreno); Linux (Docker Engine only) supports CPU, CUDA, ROCm and Vulkan. On macOS/Windows the engines run in a host sandbox, on Linux in a container. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
The Model Runner API has no authentication: any client that can reach it can pull, load and run models. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
